preamble: Correspondence of the voiced retroflex affricate [ɖʐ] (standard Polish dż) with the voiced alveolar affricate [dz] in Polish dialects with mazurzenie (Masovia, Masuria, most of Lesser Poland including the Goral area, parts of Upper Silesia), where the retroflex series /ʂ, ʐ, t͡ʂ, d͡ʐ/ merged with the dentals. Standard jeżdżę [jɛʐd͡ʐɛ] 'I drive' is [jɛzd͡zɛ] in mazurating speech, and drożdże [ˈdrɔʐ.d͡ʐɛ] 'yeast' is drozdze [ˈdrɔz.d͡zɛ] in the Zagórze dialect. The origin of mazurzenie is debated: Koneczna derives it directly from the older palato-alveolar series rather than from the retroflexes, while Kuryłowicz argues that archaic dialects replaced the new retroflexes with dentals. Old Polish historical cases such as dżban > dzban are excluded here because they predate the Polish retroflexes.

examples.note: Both ż and dż are fronted to dentals in mazurating dialects.
Wiktionary lists drozdze as the Zagórze dialect form.
